Clean pass with caveats. (1) LICENCE: the TAS-20 is copyrighted and its rights holders charge a US$40 copyright fee for the scale package (gtaylorpsychiatry.org/tas.htm, archived 2022-07-02: "A package containing a master copy of the scale, scoring instructions, reliability, validity, and normative data can be obtained upon payment of a copyright fee of US$40.00"), and they have enforced copyright to the point of a retraction (Molecular Autism, 2021: authors "did not have permission from the copyright holders to use and adapt the twenty-item Toronto Alexithymia Scale"). Under the 2026-09-04 rules in references/itemtext_standard.md this is NOT a block: no non-commercial clause and no reproduction/redistribution clause is quotable anywhere in the holders' own terms (a fee is a fee, not a prohibition -- the same reading applied to the WHOQOL royalty), and per the ECR-R ruling the licence of the source IRW copied from governs, which here is a CC BY 4.0 PeerJ deposit that published all 20 items itself in its SPSS variable labels. IRW also already ships verbatim TAS-20 wording in rmet_higgins_2022_tas (audit-confirmed green 2026-08-21). Flagging for a human because the enforcement history is real; if Ben wants the WHOQOL no-redistribution exception extended to fee-licensed instruments, this table and rmet_higgins_2022_tas are what it would withdraw. (2) The SPSS numbering is subscale-grouped, not canonical TAS-20 numbering: TAS1-7 = DIF (canonical 1,3,6,7,9,13,14), TAS8-12 = DDF (canonical 2,4,11,12,17), TAS13-20 = EOT (canonical 5,8,10,15,16,18,19,20). Item codes must not be read as canonical item numbers. (3) TAS5's label reads "I have feeling that I can't quite identify"; canonical wording is "feelings". Shipped verbatim from the source label rather than silently corrected. (4) instructions left blank: neither the paper nor the .sav publishes the administered instructions, and the canonical paper-and-pencil instruction ("circling the corresponding number") would misdescribe this online administration.
